newsitem.title: USA: RightChoice sees Q3 loss of $0.42-$0.46/shr.
newsitem.headline: RightChoice sees Q3 loss of $0.42-$0.46/shr.

text.p: RightChoice Managed Care Inc said Monday it expects to report a net loss for the third quarter of between $0.42 and $0.46 a share.
In the year-ago third quarter, RightChoice earned $0.19 a share.
It added expects a net loss in the fourth quarter.

The company said the effects of the competitive environment and higher outpatient and pharmacy utilization trends, which were previously cited, continue to pressure premium revenues and drive medical costs higher.

The company also said it plans to adjust reserve levels to meet anticipated increases in medical costs through the second half of 1996. Additional accruals to satisfy an obligation related to a third-party contract will be made as well.

"The pricing environment in 1996 has resulted in essentially flat revenue per member per month on a consolidated basis, despite growing enrollment," Frederic Brussee, president, said in a statement. "Furthermore, medical claims coming in throughout the quarter reflect the markedly higher outpatient and pharmacy benefit costs affecting the industry."
"As a result of those factors and the cyclical nature of our company's medical claims activity, we expect a third quarter medical loss ratio in a range from 88 percent to 90 percent," Brussee said.
The medical loss ratio reflects premium revenues divided by medical and health care service expenses.

RightChoice said it is trying to improve margins with initiatives on pricing, patient pre-certification procedures and reimbursement rate structures. It also is focusing on achieving more effective pharmacy benefit management through its contractor to control both utilization and drug costs.
However, until the benefits of these steps are realized, the imbalance between lower premium pricing and higher medical costs will continue to pressure margins, it added.

Managed care enrollment continues to post strong increases, including 72 percent growth in AllianceCHOICE point-of-service and 44 percent growth in BlueCHOICE and HealthNet Blue health maintenance organizations (HMO) from year-end 1995 through August 1996. Preferred provider organization (PPO) membership continues to drop, as expected.
"Margins in our HMO, along with those of our competitors, have been significantly impacted by competitive pricing pressures, especially in the St. Louis market," Brussee said.

"We do see some opportunity to improve our premium revenue levels during 1997," Brussee said. "The pricing competition is expected to ease somewhat, and approximately 50 percent of our underwritten HMO membership and 25 percent of PPO membership are eligible for re-enrollment in January 1997."

Assuming RightChoice achieved targeted re-enrollment at new price levels and increased reserves through year-end adequately reflect increases in medical costs, medical margins would be expected to stabilize in 1997, Brussee stated.
